```gherkin
Feature: System Availability and Backup

  Scenario: High Availability
    Given the system is running on the second Sunday
    When the system is under normal load
    Then the system is available with a downtime of 10 minutes

  Scenario: Daily Backup
    Given the system is running on a normal day
    When the system is backed up every night
    Then the system data is backed up every night with a cycle of 30 days

  Scenario: Rollback Provision
    Given the system is running on a normal day
    When the system is backed up every night
    Then the system can be rolled back by a month

  Scenario: Dummy Production System
    Given the system is running on a normal day
    When the system is backed up every night
    Then the dummy production system is restored with the backed up data every day

  Scenario: Dummy Production System Purge
    Given the system is running on a normal day
    When the dummy production system is restored with the backed up data every day
    Then the dummy production system is purged every day

  Scenario: Data Storage
    Given the system is running on a normal day
    When the system data is stored in Mangalore HQ
    Then the data is stored in a fireproof cabinet 25 KM away from the Hospital

  Scenario: Compliance with Healthcare Regulations
    Given the system is running on a normal day
    When the system is designed to comply with healthcare regulations
    Then the system complies with healthcare regulations as defined by the Government of India

Scenario Outline: Availability and Backup with Different Outage Windows
  Given the system is running on a normal day
  When the system is backed up every night with an outage window of <outage_window> minutes
  Then the system is available with a downtime of <outage_window> minutes

  Examples:
    | outage_window |
    | 5             |
    | 10            |
    | 15            |
    | 20            |
    | 25            |
    | 30            |
    | 35            |
    | 40            |
    | 45            |
    | 50            |

Scenario Outline: Rollback Provision with Different Backup Cycles
  Given the system is running on a normal day
  When the system is backed up every night with a cycle of <backup_cycle> days
  Then the system can be rolled back by <backup_cycle> days

  Examples:
    | backup_cycle |
    | 15           |
    | 20           |
    | 25           |
    | 30           |
    | 35           |
    | 40           |
    | 45           |
    | 50           |
    | 55           |
```
